summary: Modern data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML directly into the database layer, offering in-database model training, LLM access via SQL, and native vector search for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Gartner projects that by 2026, 30% of enterprises will rely on vector-based retrieval for GenAI (up from ~2% in 2023), and the vector database market is forecast to reach USD 17.91 billion by 2034 at a ~24% CAGR. The major platforms differ sharply on whether vector search is natively built in versus available only through extensions, and on how tightly LLMs are integrated into query workflows.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Cortex AI — managed LLM functions, embeddings, Cortex Search, and Cortex Analyst
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex provides serverless access to hosted LLMs and embedding models directly through SQL and Python, with functions like COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, and EXTRACT_ANSWER. Cortex Search delivers hybrid (semantic + keyword) retrieval, and Cortex Analyst enables natural-language querying of structured data. Snowflake Postgres also extends Cortex to Postgres applications so data can stay in Postgres while accessing AI.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type with VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY / VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE functions, and Cortex Search provides a fully managed native vector/hybrid search service.
databases.llm_integration: Deeply integrated — hosted models from Anthropic, Meta (Llama), Mistral, Snowflake Arctic, and others callable via SQL/Python without managing infrastructure.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based; Cortex functions billed in credits by tokens processed, plus serverless compute and storage. No separate AI infrastructure to manage.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML for in-database model training and Vertex AI / Gemini integration for generative AI
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets analysts create and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time-series, matrix factorization, and imported TensorFlow/ONNX models) using standard SQL. Through Vertex AI integration, BigQuery can call Gemini and other foundation models via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and generate embeddings with ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports the VECTOR_SEARCH function with vector indexes (IVF/TreeAH) for approximate nearest-neighbor search over embedding columns.
databases.llm_integration: Strong — remote models via Vertex AI (Gemini family) invoked from SQL for text generation, embeddings, and multimodal tasks.
databases.pricing_notes: Pay-as-you-go: on-demand bytes-scanned or capacity slots, plus BigQuery ML training/prediction costs and separate Vertex AI charges for generative calls.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector extension for vector storage/search and pgai for in-database LLM/embedding workflows
databases.description: PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through extensions: pgvector adds a vector data type with similarity operators and HNSW/IVFFlat indexes, while pgai (from Timescale) lets you call LLMs and generate embeddings directly from SQL, often paired with pgvectorscale for scaling. These make core Postgres a viable RAG backend.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL — vector search is provided by the third-party pgvector extension (plus pgvectorscale for performance). Core Postgres ships no built-in vector type or ANN index.
databases.llm_integration: Via the pgai extension, which integrates with OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Ollama, and others for embeddings and completions from SQL; otherwise handled in the application layer.
databases.pricing_notes: Open source and free; costs come from self-hosting/managed-provider compute and storage, plus any external LLM API usage.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning — SQL-based integration with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock/Comprehend
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you invoke ML models from SQL queries by calling SageMaker endpoints, Amazon Bedrock foundation models, and Amazon Comprehend for sentiment analysis, enriching transactional data with predictions in-line. It targets low-latency operational use cases on the Aurora OLTP engine.
databases.vector_search_notes: Aurora ML itself provides no native vector search. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL requires the pgvector extension (a third-party/community extension), so it is not a native Aurora ML capability.
databases.llm_integration: Yes — native SQL functions to call Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker endpoints, including embedding generation feeding pgvector.
databases.pricing_notes: Standard Aurora instance/storage/I-O pricing; ML inference billed separately by SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend per request/token.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML — in-warehouse model creation and inference via SageMaker Autopilot/Bedrock using SQL
databases.description: Redshift ML enables users to CREATE MODEL and run predictions with SQL; behind the scenes it uses Amazon SageMaker Autopilot to train and deploy models, and supports bringing your own models and calling Bedrock LLMs. It is optimized for analytics over large historical datasets in the Redshift warehouse.
databases.vector_search_notes: No fully native ANN vector index service dedicated to Redshift ML; Redshift has introduced vector/embedding support capabilities, but vector similarity search is not a core built-in Redshift ML feature and typically relies on integrations. Marked false for native dedicated vector search.
databases.llm_integration: Yes — SQL functions can invoke Amazon Bedrock foundation models for generative tasks and embeddings alongside SageMaker-trained models.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift compute (RPU/node) and storage pricing plus SageMaker training costs for Redshift ML models; Bedrock calls billed per token.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI for model training/serving/agents and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks Mosaic AI offers end-to-end GenAI tooling: foundation model APIs, fine-tuning, model serving, agent frameworks, and governance via Unity Catalog. Mosaic AI Vector Search is a managed vector database integrated with Delta tables that auto-syncs embeddings for RAG applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a first-party managed vector index that continuously syncs with Delta tables and performs ANN similarity search.
databases.llm_integration: Extensive — Foundation Model APIs, external model routing, fine-tuning, and agent orchestration, with open models (e.g., Llama, DBRX) and third-party models.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based DBUs for compute, model serving, and Vector Search endpoints; separate charges for foundation model token usage and serving.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search for semantic/vector retrieval integrated with the document database
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search lets you store embeddings alongside operational documents and run approximate nearest-neighbor queries using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage, supporting hybrid search and filtering. It is designed for low-latency operational AI and RAG on the same data platform as the application.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Atlas Vector Search is a built-in, fully managed vector index (HNSW-based) queried via $vectorSearch, no external extension required.
databases.llm_integration: Via integrations/frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex) and the application layer calling OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, etc.; MongoDB provides reference architectures but LLM calls occur outside the DB engine.
databases.pricing_notes: Part of Atlas; vector search runs on Search Nodes billed by instance size, plus standard Atlas cluster compute/storage. External embedding/LLM API costs are separate.
